components.text: For new colleagues, it's like a coach at your elbow. For old hands, the speed-up is small, so watch the quality.

footnote: Source: Brynjolfsson et al., arXiv preprint v2 (Nov 2024), published in QJE (2025). HBS working paper 24-013 (Sep 2023)
notes: The second finding is more interesting: the gains go mostly to beginners and to people who were weaker to begin with. In the support study, the least skilled fifth of agents resolved 36% more issues per hour. The most skilled fifth barely improved, and their resolution rates and customer satisfaction slipped a little. The consulting experiment shows the same pattern: people below average improved 43%, people above average 17%. One more figure: new agents with two months of AI performed like agents with more than six months on the job and no AI. So for new colleagues, AI is a real help. If you're experienced, don't expect it to make you much faster, and keep an eye on whether it pulls your quality down.
